To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new type of highly luminescent nanomaterial for bioimaging in which the europium(III) ion is coordinated by a water-solubilizing ligand in the presence of a hydrophobic iridium(II) complex in the pores of mesoporous silica.
a new type of highly-luminescence nanosystem was synthesized by an in situ reaction of a dinuclear iridum(III) complex and europium(III) ion within mesoporous SiO2 nanoparticles (MSNs).
we developed an efficient in-situ reaction method to synthesize a highly-luminescence Ir-Eu-MSNs for luminescent bioimagineing in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a new type of luminescent nanoparticles with special properties and their applications in bioimaging.
the development of a new generation of luminescent nanoparticles for highly sensitive and highly-contrast luminescence bioimaging.
the design of highly efficient and stable nanosystems with special photoluminescence lifetimes for bioimaging in living cells and in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the in-situ reaction of Ir-Eu complex within MSNs is a simple, effective, and versatile method to prepare a highly-luminescence nanosystem for bioimaging.
the Ir-Eu complex-sensitized MSNs are promising luminescent probes with high loading efficiency and excellent luminescence properties for luminescence bioimaging in living cells and small animals.
the Ir-Eu complex was successfully encapsulated into MSNs by an in situ reaction, which provided high luminescence intensity and high loading efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel nanosystem with high loading efficiency, bright red luminescent and special photoluminescence lifetimes.
this study provides a new strategy for in vivo luminescent bioimagination, especially for the time-gated luminscent imaging.
this is the first example of using a europium(III) luminescent probe to achieve high contrast in luminescent lymphatics imaging under visible light excitation in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the in-situ reaction of hydrophobic Ir-Eu complex and hydrophilic MSN can form a highly-luminescence nanosystem with high loading efficiency.

the use of a water-solubilized iridium(II/III)-based complex can extend the excitation window for europium(III)-emissive complexes in MSNs, which is of great significance to the development of luminescent probes for bioimaging in living systems.
the in-situ coordination reaction strategy is a promising approach to fabricate water-soluble and highly-luminescence nanoparticles with high loading efficiency for bioimaging.
